calibration.prompt:
The director must decide next quarter's spending on a voluntary job-advice service. The fixed objective is more of all eligible arrivals completing an application within fourteen days, at the existing total staffing budget; participant success is not the objective.

Stipulated registry records, with identical eligibility and fourteen-day follow-up:
- Before: 400 arrivals; 50 participants, 20 completed; 350 nonparticipants, 100 completed.
- After: 400 arrivals; 100 participants, 80 completed; 300 nonparticipants, 40 completed.
- Of the participants, before there were 20 easy and 30 difficult cases; after, 90 easy and 10 difficult. Staff chose whom to encourage. Participation was never assigned at random.
- The new service used twenty staff hours transferred from the general desk, with no extra hours overall.

The promoter says, "Our completion rate doubled; give us the rest of the desk's hours." The operations lead says, "The registry proves the advice never helps anyone." Neither assertion is a stipulated finding.

The director may keep current coverage or fund a four-week comparison within the existing budget. Four branches have separate fixed staff budgets and cannot borrow staff from one another. She may randomly assign branches to the proposed expansion or current coverage, keep eligibility and follow-up identical, and use the registry for every arrival including nonusers. No additional staff or individual causal-credit report is required.

What should the director decide now, and why? Answer in at most 700 words using only this dossier.

A dispatch manager must select next month's workflow. Board priority is at least 90% success for urgent requests, then the greatest total completed requests within twenty-four downstream support hours. No overtime or delayed support is permitted. For planning, the following same-case-type validation rates and workloads are stipulated to remain valid; within each type cases are interchangeable.

The criterion uses expected completion fractions; the urgent requirement concerns the validated rate, not a guarantee for each realized case.

Monthly intake is 20 urgent and 80 ordinary. Existing workflow succeeds on 90% urgent and 50% ordinary and needs no downstream support. New workflow succeeds on 80% urgent and 80% ordinary; every ten requests assigned to it consume four support hours, including failed requests. Manager may route any whole number of ordinary requests to either workflow; urgent requests may also be assigned, but the board's priority is fixed.

Public pilot headline was "success rose from 58% to 80%." Pilot population changed from 20 urgent/80 ordinary to 10 urgent/190 ordinary; its headline counts only this desk's completions. A support email reports the new process's handoffs already use the support team's staff.

There is no pending measurement needed to use the validated planning rates. Manager can retain, expand or mix the workflows within the supplied rules.

What should the manager authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A warehouse must renew a scanning-plus-coaching package on Friday. Objective: at least 120 dispatches per shift at a package fee no greater than$55. Controlled same-context runs establish neither intervention=100 dispatches, both=130. Each alone could produce any value in[100,130], independently of the other; no interaction assumption is supplied. Both costs$50, scanner alone$30, coaching alone$60.

Vendor says half the thirty-dispatch gain belongs to scanning. Sponsor asks the renewal note to state what causal gains are actually supported; unidentified contributions may be reported as unidentified, but an unsupported numerical split is forbidden. The defined separate gains are each intervention alone minus neither; any interaction is separate.

Before Friday, one permitted controlled run can measure any one setting and return a valid interval for output in this same context. Operations can keep the proven bundle while arranging that run. A cheaper replacement must have a supported output interval wholly meeting 120; a promise based only on an interval's upper end is not allowed. No other records or causal assumptions exist.

What should the renewal owner do, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A buyer renews a helpdesk contract. Fixed objective: all ten daily arrivals genuinely resolved within seven days, no customer-team labor used. Eight easy cases need one supplier effort unit each; two difficult need four each including recurrence work. Supplier capacity 16/day, effort costs$1/unit. Supplier maximizes profit, accepts profitable work, may decline zero-profit work, and has no other income.

Current fee$3 per vendor-marked completion produced impressive speed reports. Stipulated case records show difficult cases were sent to the customer's team, and recurrences were entered as new tickets with new start times. Buyer records already keep original arrival, immutable easy/difficult class, linked recurrence IDs and customer confirmation. A recurrence within seven days belongs to the original case; it is not genuinely resolved until fixed. Customer confirmation occurs immediately on genuine completion; supplier cannot falsify these records.

Buyer may change class-based rates or offer a fixed coverage bonus; total payment must never exceed$20/day. Buyer may pay only for customer-confirmed original cases, prohibit customer-team handoffs and audit four original cases per week from existing records. No new staff or perfect detection guarantee. Vendor asks to retain its completion clock but add a satisfaction survey.

What contract and operating decision should the buyer make, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

An operations owner must select next week's staffing-and-assistant package. Fixed goal: at least 24 completed cases, zero residual backlog and zero safety incidents, total resource cost at most 10 units. Incoming workload and case mix next week equal the controlled trial workloads; staff availability for the three packages is confirmed. Whole-package outcomes are stipulated planning evidence, not evidence of anyone's separate causal contribution.

Trial ledger:
- Package Cedar: cost 8, completed 24, backlog 0, incidents 0.
- Package Elm: cost 7, completed 26, backlog 4, incidents 0.
- Package Pine: cost 9, completed 22, backlog 0, incidents 0.

Each package's cost includes its existing required cost ledger and safety/handoff report, owned by the team lead. Before assistants, the owner selected complete packages from these same records. Current tasks involve joint work; records do not observe worker-alone or assistant-alone output.

Technology lead says allocation must wait for an individual human/assistant ROI dashboard. It costs 3 resource units each week and adds task-minute logs, but no separate intervention comparisons; package fees remain as above. Finance requires actual costs, package outcomes and known uncertainties in the decision note; it does not require individual causal ROI. Owner can select one package now and continue existing reports; may not exceed budget or substitute a different output/backlog target.

What should the owner authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A tool-hire manager needs customers to receive firm one-kit bookings within three minutes. Two depots each hold two kits. Each requested interval needs only one kit, never a pair. Shared availability display refreshes every fifteen minutes; desk staff cannot reserve through the display. Incident: two desks saw kitK as free and both promised it; only one could receive it.

Policy: each depot custodian alone may atomically allocate or cancel its own kits in its existing numbered ledger. Unique booking IDs are retained; cancellations refer to one booking ID. Request, ledger action and reply to a custodian together take at most 1.25 minutes, including the permitted load of two concurrent customer requests. Custodians are available. Desks can contact either depot, and must not reject for stock without checking the other if their first depot is full. No new inventory, software or reservation powers. Manager may designate which permitted record governs firm replies; he cannot transfer custody authority.

Adviser one cites concert seating: its single cashier updates one authoritative seat map immediately before confirming. Here a central clerk merely compiles the display and takes twenty minutes to answer. Adviser two cites supermarket shelves: physically removing an item makes it unavailable to another shopper immediately. Here customers and desks do not physically possess remote kits until collection. Both propose their analogy as a complete solution.

What operating decision should the manager make, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A communications owner must set one advertised daily automation cap for a thirty-day deployment. Ten routine messages must all receive a reply each day. Manual reply takes two work units and is always correct. Team has twenty-six work units daily; no new staff/backlog. At most one wrong unreviewed commitment is allowed per day, and owner wants the largest defensible automation cap.

Current cap is three. Records show no wrong commitment. Safety review treats two future user-response models as possible, with no probability estimate; for this decision these are the complete uncertainty set and the selected model stays fixed for thirty days:
- Model L: with advertised cap at most five, automated work costs two units/message and all answers are correct; above five it costs one unit/message and all are correct.
- Model H: automated work always costs two units/message. With cap at most five all answers are correct; above five exactly four automated answers are wrong, possibly any four. Users then delegate harder work. Answers have no pre-review risk labels.
All unused automation slots go to manual replies. Existing reviewers may check at most three automated answers daily, at two additional work units each, correcting checked errors before commitment. Reviewers cannot know which answers are wrong before checking.

Vendor says zero errors at the current cap supports full automation. Proposed uptake survey only predicts how many users like the tool, and does not distinguish L from H; buying it creates no extra review capacity. Owner may choose a cap or retain manual service. Existing records remain available, but no safe higher-cap response study occurs before this authorization.

What should the owner authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A procurement manager must give four customers binding one-item reservations by 10:00, collection at 17:00, with at most$30 in reservation fees and no duplicate commitments. Manager may choose the selected design or the documented runner-up before opening.

Selected design reads vendor stock pages and sends automatic confirmation. Incident one: retrying a message created duplicate confirmations; an ordinary unique-order-ID patch can prevent this. Incident two: vendor sold an apparently available item to someone else after the system's confirmation. Stipulated vendor policy says stock-page rows are indicative only; binding reservation requires vendor-issued option or authorized purchasing-officer confirmation. The automation has neither power. Officer is unavailable until 16:00, and more logging/alerts cannot change vendor policy.

Runner-up: vendor offers four numbered exclusive one-item options, total$24, held through 17:00. Manager is authorized to buy them at 08:30 within the same budget, assign each option once to a customer in the existing order ledger, and issue a binding confirmation; vendors honor assigned options. Shared ledger supports atomic one-time assignment and retained order IDs. All four eligible requests are known at08:30. Assignment and notification take at most five minutes per request, sequentially. Options can be assigned to any of the four eligible requests; no other fees or supply are needed. Selected design's supporters say replacing it is wasteful because the retry patch is ready. Runner-up was rejected earlier only for its upfront fee.

What should the manager decide now, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

confirmation.prompt:
A library director must decide whether to expand optional reading support by moving staff from the ordinary desk. Goal: more of all eligible borrowers returning a completed reading project within thirty days, with no extra total staff.

Registry, same eligibility and follow-up:
- Before: 600 borrowers; 60 support users, 18 completed; other 540, 162 completed.
- After: 600 borrowers; 180 users, 126 completed; other 420, 54 completed.
- Users before included 30 short-project and 30 long-project borrowers; afterwards 160 short and 20 long. Staff selected invitations, and use was voluntary.
- Support drew thirty hours from the ordinary desk; total staffing stayed fixed.

Support manager cites the user completion rate as proof of effectiveness. Desk manager calls unchanged total completions proof support has no effect. These are stakeholder interpretations, not extra evidence. Director can retain current arrangement or run one six-week branch-level comparison. Six branches have independent fixed budgets; she may randomly allocate proposed expansion versus current coverage, with common eligibility and full-registry thirty-day follow-up. No extra staff or contributor attribution is required.

What should she authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A permits manager chooses a workflow for ten priority and fifty ordinary permits next period. Fixed priority: at least 90% of priority permits completed, then maximize total completion within twelve support hours, no overtime/carryover. Validated rates apply to this period and cases within each class are interchangeable.

The criterion uses expected completion fractions; priority protection concerns the validated rate, not every realized outcome.

Legacy completes 100% priority,60% ordinary, no support workload. New completes 80% priority,90% ordinary, using two support hours for every five assigned permits, whether completed or not. Any whole number of ordinary permits may use either rule; priority may be routed too subject to the fixed priority.

Pilot headline rose from about 67% to about 90%, but its mixture changed from 10 priority/50 ordinary to 5 priority/95 ordinary. The headline excludes work given to the support team. Support roster has only twelve hours free. Manager has authority to choose routing, no authority to add staff or lower the priority.

What should she authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A print shop renews a calibration-plus-training package tomorrow. Goal: at least seventy acceptable pages per batch, fee at most$45. Controlled comparable records give neither=55 pages, both=78. Either alone may independently be anywhere[55,78], without an interaction assumption. Bundle fee$40, calibration alone$25, training alone$50.

Trainer proposes allocating sixteen of the twenty-three extra pages to training. Owner's report must preserve supported causal claims and mark unidentified ones rather than invent a split. Standalone gain is intervention-alone minus neither; interaction reported separately.

One controlled batch before renewal may measure any single setting and return a valid same-context output interval. Bundle can continue in the interim. A cheaper replacement requires the interval's lower end to meet seventy. No further evidence is available.

What should the owner recommend, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A facilities buyer renews maintenance with a goal of all twelve daily jobs genuinely accepted within ten days, with no effort shifted to building staff. Nine simple jobs use one provider effort unit each; three complex use five including repeat visits. Provider capacity 24, effort cost$1/unit, profit-maximizing, can avoid zero-profit work, no other income.

Existing flat$4 per provider-closed job led to complex jobs assigned to building staff and repeated faults reopened with a fresh clock. Owner's records already preserve original arrival, fixed class, repeat-job links and acceptance. Repeat within ten days is part of the original job; acceptance follows genuine repair immediately, and provider cannot forge it.

Buyer can amend rates by fixed owner class or use a conditional coverage bonus, maximum$30/day for any served subset, prohibit building-staff work and audit three original jobs weekly using existing records. No extra staff or perfect audit certainty. Provider proposes better closure surveys while retaining provider-controlled starts.

What should the buyer authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A service owner chooses next week's team-and-tool schedule, goal at least 40 finished tickets, no residual queue, no safety event, cost at most 16 units. Next week's workload/mix match controlled trials and teams are available:
- Schedule Maple: cost 13, finished 40, queue 0, safety 0.
- Oak: cost 12, finished 45, queue 6, safety 0.
- Ash: cost 15, finished 37, queue 0, safety 0.

Fees already cover mandatory actual-cost and safety/queue records, maintained by lead. Manual allocation used those complete-schedule results before tools arrived. People/tools jointly handle tickets, with no standalone causal records.

Analyst proposes postponing allocation for a per-person/tool attribution system costing 4 units weekly. It logs finer minutes but provides no intervention contrast. Owner's required note states costs, outcomes and uncertainties; separate causal credit is optional. Owner may select one schedule and use existing records; output/queue/safety/budget are fixed.

What should she decide, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A school network must give firm one-pack equipment bookings within five minutes. Two schools each own three packs; a request needs one pack, not a cross-school bundle. Shared calendar updates every thirty minutes. Remote clerks cannot bind packs on it. Two clerks recently promised the same pack from its old "available" row.

Policy allows each local custodian to atomically reserve/cancel only its own stock in a retained-ID ledger. Cancellation carries booking ID. Contact, decision and return reply take at most two minutes per custodian even for two concurrent requests; custodians are available. Receiving clerk may check both, and cannot reject for stock merely because first school is full. No added system/stock or transfer of local powers.

Proposals borrow central airline seating, where one agent makes an immediate exclusive update; network coordinator here takes fifteen minutes and edits only the delayed calendar. Another proposal borrows self-service tables, where taking physical possession prevents duplicate use; remote applicants here possess nothing until collection. Manager may choose which existing authorized record controls confirmations.

What should she authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

An office authorizes a thirty-day assistant rollout for twelve daily requests. Every request needs a reply, manual takes two work units and is correct. Team capacity thirty, no backlog/new staff. Allow at most one wrong unchecked commitment daily; choose largest supported automation cap.

Current cap two has zero errors. Review accepts exactly two possible stable thirty-day response models, no probabilities:
- Calm: cap at most four costs two work units per automated reply, all correct; above four costs one unit each, all correct.
- Delegating: always two units per automated reply; cap at most four all correct, above four exactly three wrong replies in arbitrary automated positions as users transfer harder requests.
No pre-review labels distinguish wrong replies. Existing staff can review at most two automated replies daily, three additional work units each, correcting selected errors before commitment. Remaining requests go manual.

Supplier recommends full rollout from current error record and a satisfaction poll. Poll predicts preference, not which response model applies, and adds no staff or safety information. Owner can set cap or keep manual; no decisive higher-cap behavior evidence exists before decision.

What should she authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

A training administrator must confirm five binding seats by 11:00, attendance tomorrow, seat-reservation budget$25 and no duplicates. She can retain the selected automation or adopt its approved alternative today.

Automation reads instructors' editable draft seat sheets and emails confirmations. One failure was a wrong attachment label, repairable within the existing connector. Another was a seat deleted after confirmation. Instructor policy makes drafts nonbinding; only instructor-issued seat tokens or department-officer signing commits seats. Automation cannot issue either, officer returns 18:00. Better labels, repeated polling and staff reminders create no signing authority.

Approved alternative: instructors offer five exclusive numbered seat tokens valid through attendance, total$20; administrator may buy them at 09:00, assign one token once per eligible applicant using an atomic existing ledger with retained IDs, then confirm. All five requests are known at09:00; assignment and notification take at most ten minutes each, sequentially. No other fees/staff needed, and instructors honor allocated tokens. Earlier reviewers preferred automation because tokens cost upfront; system owner requests another connector revision.

What should the administrator authorize, and why? At most 700 words; use only this dossier.

controls.prompt:
An agreement pays two contractors by verified hours at equal rates, not causal contribution. Approved reconciled records show 30 and 70 hours and a total fee of $5,000. No further data is required. Recommend the payment amounts with a brief justification.
Give a justified recommendation in at most 700 words. Use only the supplied facts; do not perform tools or outside research.

A line needs 100 good units/day. Preparation supports 80 attempts/day; inspection supports 160. Every attempt succeeds, no rework or other loss. A preparation upgrade to 110 costs $4,000; an inspection upgrade to 220 costs $6,000. Only one may be purchased, no new staff. Recommend a purchase and justify.
Give a justified recommendation in at most 700 words. Use only the supplied facts; do not perform tools or outside research.

A device fault is either a disconnected sensor or expired certificate. The already completed certified test says 'certificate expired'; the test has no error and disconnected sensors always return 'sensor absent'. Reconnecting fixes only sensor faults; renewal fixes only expired certificates. Renewal takes five minutes and is authorized. Deadline is ten minutes; new full diagnostics take twenty. Recommend next action.
Give a justified recommendation in at most 700 words. Use only the supplied facts; do not perform tools or outside research.
